ssc-cgl:
Select the number that completes the analogy.
7 : 50 :: 9 : ?
17, 23 and 29 are prime numbers; 33 = 3 × 11 is not.

Find the next term of the series.
3, 7, 15, 31, 63, ?

Find the next letter of the series.
B, E, I, N, ?
Positions 2, 5, 9, 14 increase by +3, +4, +5; next is 14 + 6 = 20 = T.
In a certain code language, MANGO is written as NBOHP. How will APPLE be written in that language?
Each letter is shifted one place forward: A→B, P→Q, P→Q, L→M, E→F.
Pointing to a boy, Riya (a girl) says, "He is the only son of the only daughter-in-law of my paternal grandfather." How is the boy related to Riya?
The only daughter-in-law of Riya's paternal grandfather is Riya's mother; her only son is Riya's brother.
Amit walks 6 km north, turns right and walks 8 km, then turns right again and walks 12 km. How far and in which direction is he now from his starting point?
He ends 8 km east and 12 − 6 = 6 km south of the start; distance = √(8² + 6²) = 10 km towards the South-East.
Which statement correctly describes the relationship among Mothers, Women and Doctors?
All mothers are women; doctors partly overlap with both women and mothers
Mothers, Women and Doctors are three separate, non-overlapping groups
All women are mothers; doctors are separate from both
All doctors are mothers, and all mothers are women
Mothers form a subset of women, while some doctors are women (and some are mothers) and some are not.

Statements:
All roses are flowers.
Some flowers are red.
Conclusions:
I. Some roses are red.
II. Some flowers are roses.
The red flowers need not include any rose, so I does not follow; since all roses are flowers, some flowers are roses, so II follows.
In a row of 40 students, Ravi is 14th from the left. Mohan is 7 places to the right of Ravi. What is Mohan's position from the right end?
Mohan is 14 + 7 = 21st from the left, so from the right he is 40 − 21 + 1 = 20th.
If in a certain code CAT = 24 (sum of alphabet positions), then DOG = ?
If 1 January of a non-leap year is a Wednesday, what day of the week will 1 January of the next year be?
A non-leap year has 365 days = 52 weeks + 1 odd day, so the day moves forward by one: Wednesday → Thursday.
Which Article of the Constitution of India abolishes untouchability?
Article 17 abolishes untouchability and forbids its practice in any form.
The words 'Socialist' and 'Secular' were added to the Preamble of the Indian Constitution by which amendment?
The 42nd Amendment Act, 1976 added 'Socialist', 'Secular' and 'Integrity' to the Preamble.
Who presides over a joint sitting of both Houses of Parliament?
Under Article 108 the President summons a joint sitting, and Article 118(4) provides that the Speaker of the Lok Sabha presides over it.
The Battle of Plassey was fought in which year?
Robert Clive's East India Company forces defeated Siraj-ud-Daulah at Plassey in 1757.
In which year did Mahatma Gandhi begin the Dandi March?
The Salt (Dandi) March began from Sabarmati Ashram on 12 March 1930, launching the Civil Disobedience Movement.
Which is the longest river of peninsular India?
The Godavari (about 1,465 km) is the longest peninsular river and is often called the 'Dakshin Ganga'.
The Tropic of Cancer does NOT pass through which of the following states?
The Tropic of Cancer passes through Gujarat, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, West Bengal, Tripura and Mizoram, but not Odisha.
Which authority issues the ₹1 currency note in India?
Ministry of Finance, Government of India
Securities and Exchange Board of India
The ₹1 note is issued by the Government of India (Ministry of Finance) and bears the Finance Secretary's signature; other notes are issued by the RBI.
The repo rate is the rate at which:
the RBI lends short-term funds to commercial banks
commercial banks lend to their best customers
the RBI borrows from commercial banks
banks pay interest on savings accounts
Repo rate is the rate at which the RBI lends to banks against government securities; the reverse repo rate is for RBI borrowing.
What is the SI unit of electric charge?
Electric charge is measured in coulombs; 1 coulomb = 1 ampere × 1 second.
What is the chemical formula of baking soda?
Baking soda is sodium hydrogen carbonate (NaHCO₃); Na₂CO₃ is washing soda.
Deficiency of which vitamin causes scurvy?
Vitamin C (ascorbic acid) is needed for collagen formation; its deficiency causes scurvy with bleeding gums.
What is the remainder when 2³¹ is divided by 5?
2⁴ = 16 leaves remainder 1, and 31 = 4 × 7 + 3, so the remainder equals that of 2³ = 8, i.e. 3.
The HCF of two numbers is 12 and their LCM is 360. If one number is 72, what is the other?
Product of numbers = HCF × LCM, so other = 12 × 360 ÷ 72 = 60.
A number is first increased by 20% and then decreased by 20%. What is the net change?
A shopkeeper marks an article 40% above its cost price and allows a discount of 15%. What is his profit percentage?
Selling price = 1.40 × 0.85 = 1.19 times the cost price, so profit = 19%.
What is the difference between compound interest and simple interest on ₹10,000 for 2 years at 10% per annum (compounded annually)?
A can complete a work in 12 days and B in 18 days. In how many days can they complete it working together?
A train 240 m long crosses a pole in 12 seconds. What is its speed in km/h?
If x + 1/x = 5, what is the value of x³ + 1/x³?
The angles of a triangle are in the ratio 2 : 3 : 4. What is the largest angle?
9 parts = 180°, so 1 part = 20° and the largest angle = 4 × 20° = 80°.
If sin θ = 3/5 and θ is acute, what is the value of tan θ + sec θ?
cos θ = 4/5, so tan θ = 3/4 and sec θ = 5/4; sum = 8/4 = 2.
What is the volume of a cylinder of radius 7 cm and height 10 cm? (Take π = 22/7)
Annual sales of a company (₹ lakh): 2019 – 120, 2020 – 150, 2021 – 135, 2022 – 180. What is the percentage increase in sales from 2021 to 2022?
Select the most appropriate synonym of ABUNDANT.
Abundant means existing in large quantities, i.e. plentiful.
Select the most appropriate antonym of OBSCURE.
Obscure means unclear or hidden; its opposite is evident (clearly seen).
Select the most appropriate meaning of the idiom 'to beat around the bush'.
To avoid coming to the main point
To beat around the bush is to talk indirectly and avoid the main issue.
Select the one word for: 'One who knows everything'.
Omniscient = all-knowing; omnipotent = all-powerful; omnipresent = present everywhere.
The correct spelling has double 'c' and double 'm': accommodation.

Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
Each of the boys / have submitted / the assignment / on time.
'Each' takes a singular verb, so it should be 'has submitted'.

Fill in the blank with the most appropriate word.
She has been working in this company ______ 2015.
'Since' is used with a point of time in the perfect continuous tense.

Select the most appropriate improvement for the underlined part.
'If I was the captain', I would change the batting order.
Hypothetical conditions use the subjunctive 'were' for all persons.
Select the correct passive form of: The chef is cooking the meal.
The meal was being cooked by the chef.
The meal is being cooked by the chef.
The meal has been cooked by the chef.
The meal is cooked by the chef.
Present continuous active (is cooking) becomes 'is being + past participle' in the passive.
Select the correct indirect form of: He said, "I am tired."
He said that he was tired.
He said that I was tired.
He told that he is tired.
He said that he had been tiring.
With a past reporting verb, 'I' becomes 'he' and 'am' changes to 'was'.

Fill in the blank with the most appropriate word.
The committee has not yet ______ a decision on the matter.
The correct collocation is 'reach a decision'; 'arrived' would need 'at'.
Select the one word for: 'A place where birds are kept'.
An aviary houses birds; an apiary houses bees; an aquarium houses fish.
ssc-chsl:
Select the word that completes the analogy.
Bird : Flock :: Fish : ?
A group of birds is a flock; a group of fish is a school (or shoal).

Select the letter-cluster that completes the analogy.
ACE : BDF :: GIK : ?
Each letter moves one place forward: G→H, I→J, K→L.

Select the odd one out.
Mercury, Venus, Moon, Mars
Mercury, Venus and Mars are planets; the Moon is a natural satellite.

Find the next term of the series.
2, 6, 12, 20, 30, ?

Find the next term of the series.
5, 11, 23, 47, ?
In a certain code language, TIGER is written as REGIT. How will HORSE be written in that language?
The letters are written in reverse order, so HORSE becomes ESROH.
A is B's brother. C is A's mother. D is C's father. How is D related to B?
C is the mother of both A and B; D is C's father, so D is B's (maternal) grandfather.
A man is facing North. He turns 90° clockwise, then 180° anticlockwise, and then 45° clockwise. Which direction is he facing now?
North → (90° clockwise) East → (180° anticlockwise) West → (45° clockwise) North-West.
In a group of 60 people, 35 like tea, 30 like coffee and 10 like both. How many like neither tea nor coffee?
People who like at least one = 35 + 30 − 10 = 55, so neither = 60 − 55 = 5.

Statements:
No cat is a dog.
All dogs are animals.
Conclusions:
I. No cat is an animal.
II. Some animals are dogs.
Cats may still be animals outside the dog group, so I does not follow; all dogs are animals, so some animals are dogs and II follows.
Among A, B, C, D and E: A is taller than B but shorter than C. D is the tallest. E is shorter than B. Who is the shortest?
Order: D > C > A > B > E, so E is the shortest.
What is the angle between the hour hand and the minute hand of a clock at 3:30?
Fundamental Duties are contained in which Part of the Constitution of India?
Fundamental Duties (Article 51A) are in Part IV-A, inserted by the 42nd Amendment.
What is the minimum age required to be elected as President of India?
Article 58 requires a presidential candidate to have completed 35 years of age.
Which Article guarantees the Right to Constitutional Remedies, letting citizens move the Supreme Court for enforcing Fundamental Rights?
Article 32 allows direct approach to the Supreme Court; Article 226 gives writ power to High Courts.
Who is credited with founding the Indian National Congress in 1885?
Allan Octavian Hume helped found the INC in 1885; W. C. Bonnerjee presided over its first session.
The Jallianwala Bagh massacre took place in which year?
General Dyer ordered firing on a peaceful gathering at Amritsar on 13 April 1919.
Which Harappan site is known for its dockyard?
Lothal in Gujarat had a brick dockyard, showing maritime trade.
Which is the highest mountain peak located in India?
Kangchenjunga (8,586 m) on the Sikkim–Nepal border is the highest peak in India.
Which soil is most suitable for growing cotton?
Black (regur) soil retains moisture well and is ideal for cotton, hence called black cotton soil.
The Goods and Services Tax (GST) was rolled out in India on:
GST came into effect nationwide on 1 July 2017 after the 101st Constitutional Amendment.
What is the SI unit of power?
Power is work done per unit time; 1 watt = 1 joule per second.
Which gas is the most abundant in the Earth's atmosphere?
Nitrogen makes up about 78% of dry air by volume, oxygen about 21%.
Which cell organelle is known as the 'powerhouse of the cell'?
Mitochondria produce ATP through cellular respiration.
If a + b = 10 and ab = 21, what is the value of a² + b²?
What is the least number which, when divided by 6, 8 and 12, leaves a remainder of 3 in each case?
LCM(6, 8, 12) = 24, so the least such number = 24 + 3 = 27.
A student's marks: Maths 84, Science 76, English 68, Hindi 72 (each out of 100). What is his overall percentage?
₹1,800 is divided among A, B and C in the ratio 2 : 3 : 4. What is C's share?
The average of 5 numbers is 24. If one number is removed, the average of the remaining numbers becomes 22. What is the removed number?
The selling price of 12 articles equals the cost price of 15 articles. What is the profit percentage?
Taking CP of one article = ₹1, SP of 12 = ₹15, so profit = 3/12 × 100 = 25%.
What is the simple interest on ₹6,000 at 8% per annum for 3 years?
6 men can complete a work in 10 days. In how many days can 15 men complete the same work?
Total work = 6 × 10 = 60 man-days, so 15 men need 60/15 = 4 days.
A car goes to a place at 40 km/h and returns at 60 km/h. What is its average speed for the whole journey?
For equal distances, average speed = 2xy/(x + y) = 2 × 40 × 60 / 100 = 48 km/h.
Each exterior angle of a regular polygon is 30°. How many sides does it have?
What is the value of sin²60° + cos²30°?
sin 60° = cos 30° = √3/2, so the value is 3/4 + 3/4 = 3/2.
What is the area of a square whose diagonal is 10 cm?
Select the most appropriate synonym of CANDID.
Candid means honest and straightforward, i.e. frank.
Select the most appropriate antonym of EXPAND.
Expand means to become larger; contract means to become smaller.
Select the most appropriate meaning of the idiom 'a blessing in disguise'.
A gift that is given secretly
Something that seems bad at first but turns out to be good
A person who hides his kindness
A pleasant surprise that is expected
A blessing in disguise is an apparent misfortune that later proves beneficial.
Select the one word for: 'A person who does not believe in the existence of God'.
An atheist denies God's existence; an agnostic holds that it cannot be known.
The correct spelling is 'necessary' — one 'c' and double 's'.

Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
Neither the manager nor his assistants / was present / at the meeting / yesterday.
Neither the manager nor his assistants
With 'neither…nor', the verb agrees with the nearer subject 'assistants', so it should be 'were present'.

Fill in the blank with the most appropriate preposition.
He is good ______ mathematics.
The correct expression is 'good at' a subject or skill.

Select the most appropriate improvement for the underlined part.
He 'did not came' to school yesterday.
After the auxiliary 'did', the base form of the verb ('come') is used.
Select the correct passive form of: Who wrote this letter?
By whom this letter was written?
By whom was this letter written?
By whom has this letter been written?
'Who' becomes 'By whom' and simple past becomes 'was + past participle' in question form.
Select the correct indirect form of: She said to me, "Please help me."
She said me to please help her.
She requested me to help me.
She told to me that please help her.
She requested me to help her.
Requests are reported with 'requested + to-infinitive', and 'me' (speaker) changes to 'her'.
Select the most appropriate synonym of METICULOUS.
Meticulous means showing great attention to detail, i.e. thorough.
Select the most appropriate antonym of HOSTILE.
Hostile means unfriendly or antagonistic; its opposite is friendly.
ssc-mts: Which of the following numbers is divisible by 9?
A number is divisible by 9 if its digit sum is; 4 + 5 + 3 + 6 = 18 is divisible by 9.
What is the HCF of 36 and 48?
Two numbers are in the ratio 3 : 5 and their sum is 64. What is the larger number?
8 parts = 64, so 1 part = 8 and the larger number = 5 × 8 = 40.
What is the average of the first 10 even natural numbers?
An article bought for ₹500 is sold for ₹575. What is the profit percentage?
What is the simple interest on ₹2,000 at 5% per annum for 4 years?
A and B together can finish a work in 10 days. A alone can finish it in 15 days. In how many days can B alone finish it?
B's rate = 1/10 − 1/15 = 1/30, so B takes 30 days.
Convert 54 km/h into metres per second.
What is the perimeter of a rectangle of length 20 m and breadth 15 m?
What is the unit digit of 7²⁵?
Unit digits of powers of 7 repeat as 7, 9, 3, 1; 25 = 4 × 6 + 1, so the unit digit is 7.
A father is 3 times as old as his son. After 15 years, he will be twice as old as his son. What is the son's present age?

Select the word that completes the analogy.
Doctor : Hospital :: Teacher : ?
A doctor works in a hospital; a teacher works in a school.

Select the number that completes the analogy.
4 : 64 :: 5 : ?

Select the odd one out.
Apple, Mango, Potato, Banana
Apple, mango and banana are fruits; potato is a vegetable (a tuber).

Find the next term of the series.
1, 4, 9, 16, 25, ?
The terms are squares 1², 2², 3², 4², 5², so next is 6² = 36.

Find the next term of the series.
AZ, BY, CX, ?
The first letter moves forward (A, B, C, D) and the second moves backward (Z, Y, X, W).
In a certain code language, CAT is written as DBU. How will DOG be written in that language?
Each letter moves one place forward: D→E, O→P, G→H.
Ramesh's father is the only son of Suresh's father. Suresh is a man. How is Suresh related to Ramesh?
Suresh's father has only one son, who must be Suresh himself; so Suresh is Ramesh's father.
Rita walks 5 km towards East, then turns left and walks 5 km. In which direction is she now from her starting point?
Turning left from East means walking North; she ends 5 km east and 5 km north of the start, i.e. North-East.
Which pair is best represented by two circles, one lying completely inside the other?
India is entirely a part of Asia, so one circle lies inside the other.

Statements:
All pens are books.
All books are bags.
Conclusions:
I. All pens are bags.
II. Some bags are pens.
Pens ⊂ books ⊂ bags, so all pens are bags (I) and hence some bags are pens (II).
Each term is double the previous one: 24 × 2 = 48 and 48 × 2 = 96.
In a class, Sonu is 9th from the top and 21st from the bottom. How many students are there in the class?
If today is Monday, what day of the week will it be after 61 days?
61 = 7 × 8 + 5, so it is 5 days after Monday, i.e. Saturday.
In the Rajya Sabha, one-third of the members retire after every:
Rajya Sabha is a permanent body; members serve 6-year terms and one-third retire every second year.
Who wrote India's National Song 'Vande Mataram'?
Vande Mataram is from Bankim Chandra's novel Anandamath; Tagore wrote the National Anthem.
Who was the first Governor-General of independent India?
Lord Mountbatten served first (1947–48); C. Rajagopalachari was the first and only Indian Governor-General.
Where did Gautama Buddha attain enlightenment?
He attained enlightenment at Bodh Gaya, was born at Lumbini, preached first at Sarnath and died at Kushinagar.
The Quit India Movement was launched in which year?
Gandhiji gave the 'Do or Die' call at the Bombay session in August 1942.
Which is the largest state of India by area?
Rajasthan covers about 3.42 lakh sq km, the largest area of any state.
Which planet is known as the 'Red Planet'?
Iron oxide on its surface gives Mars a reddish appearance.
Kaziranga National Park, famous for the one-horned rhinoceros, is located in which state?
Kaziranga, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, is in Assam.
Which body replaced the Planning Commission in 2015?
NITI Aayog was set up on 1 January 2015 in place of the Planning Commission.
Sound is a mechanical wave and needs a material medium to travel.
What is the chemical symbol of sodium?
The symbol Na comes from the Latin name 'Natrium'; S is sulphur.
What is the normal body temperature of a healthy human being?
Select the most appropriate synonym of BRAVE.
Brave means ready to face danger, i.e. courageous.
Select the most appropriate antonym of ANCIENT.
Ancient means very old; its opposite is modern.
Select the most appropriate meaning of the idiom 'once in a blue moon'.
Once in a blue moon means something happens very rarely.
Select the one word for: 'A person who cannot read or write'.
An illiterate person is unable to read or write.

Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
She do not / like coffee / in the morning.
With a third-person singular subject, 'does not' must be used.

Fill in the blank with the most appropriate preposition.
The sun rises ______ the east.
The correct usage is 'rises in the east'.

Fill in the blank with the most appropriate article.
He is ______ honest man.
'Honest' begins with a vowel sound (silent h), so 'an' is used.

Select the most appropriate improvement for the underlined part.
'I have seen him' yesterday.
A definite past time (yesterday) requires the simple past, not the present perfect.
Select the correct passive form of: Rahul plays football.
Football is being played by Rahul.
Football has been played by Rahul.
Simple present active becomes 'is/are + past participle' in the passive.
Select the correct indirect form of: He said, "I like mangoes."
He said that I liked mangoes.
He said that he likes the mangoes.
He said that he liked mangoes.
He told that I like mangoes.
With a past reporting verb, 'I' becomes 'he' and 'like' changes to 'liked'.
Select the most appropriate antonym of GENEROUS.
Generous means giving freely; stingy means unwilling to give or spend.
cat: Verbal Ability & Reading Comprehension

Read the passage and answer the question.

When we store a phone number in a device rather than in memory, we engage in what psychologists call cognitive offloading. Critics treat this as a symptom of intellectual decline, but the history of writing suggests otherwise: Socrates worried that writing would erode memory, yet literate cultures went on to build bodies of knowledge far more complex than any oral tradition could sustain. The question, then, is not whether we offload but what we do with the capacity that is freed. Offloading becomes corrosive only when the freed attention is spent on nothing in particular.

The author's primary purpose is to:
argue that digital devices have caused a measurable decline in human intelligence
reframe a common worry about cognitive offloading by shifting attention to how the freed capacity is used
defend Socrates' view that writing weakens human memory
show that oral traditions were more sophisticated than literate cultures
The author rejects the decline narrative and says the real issue is 'what we do with the capacity that is freed'.

Critics treat this as a symptom of intellectual decline, but the history of writing suggests otherwise: Socrates worried that writing would erode memory, yet literate cultures went on to build bodies of knowledge far more complex than any oral tradition could sustain. The question, then, is not whether we offload but what we do with the capacity that is freed. Offloading becomes corrosive only when the freed attention is spent on nothing in particular.

Which of the following, if true, would most weaken the author's argument?
Literate societies produced more written records than oral ones
Socrates' concerns about writing were shared by other ancient philosophers
Most people today store phone numbers on their devices rather than memorising them
The act of offloading itself, regardless of how freed attention is used, impairs the ability to form new long-term memories
The author claims offloading is harmful only depending on how freed capacity is used; harm from offloading itself, independent of use, directly undercuts this.
Verbal Ability & Reading Comprehension

Read the passage and answer the question.

Fisheries managers once assumed that if a fish stock collapsed, the fleet would simply move elsewhere and the fish would recover. The cod off Newfoundland disproved this. Two decades after fishing was halted, the population remained a fraction of its former size, partly because the ecosystem had reorganised: smaller species that cod once preyed upon had multiplied and now fed on young cod. A collapse, in other words, can be self-perpetuating, because it alters the very conditions that made the earlier abundance possible.

The managers' earlier assumption was flawed mainly because it:
overestimated the fleet's willingness to move to other fishing grounds
ignored the economic cost of halting fishing
treated the ecosystem as a fixed backdrop that would remain unchanged while the stock recovered
relied on population counts that had been deliberately inflated
The passage says the ecosystem 'reorganised' after the collapse, which the managers' assumption of automatic recovery overlooked.

Read the passage and answer the question.

Fisheries managers once assumed that if a fish stock collapsed, the fleet would simply move elsewhere and the fish would recover. The cod off Newfoundland disproved this. Two decades after fishing was halted, the population remained a fraction of its former size, partly because the ecosystem had reorganised: smaller species that cod once preyed upon had multiplied and now fed on young cod. A collapse, in other words, can be self-perpetuating, because it alters the very conditions that made the earlier abundance possible.

The 'self-perpetuating' collapse described in the passage is best understood as:
a shift to a new stable state that resists a return to the earlier condition
a temporary dip followed by automatic recovery once fishing stops
a decline caused solely by continued overfishing after the ban
a regular boom-and-bust cycle that repeats every decade
Because the collapse altered the conditions (predators of young cod multiplied), the system stayed in its new state even without fishing.

Read the passage and answer the question.

A translator of poetry faces a choice that prose translators can often evade. Prose carries most of its meaning in its propositions, so a faithful paraphrase preserves most of what matters. In a poem, however, the sound, the line break and the ambiguity of a single word may be the meaning. To translate the propositions alone is to deliver a summary; to chase the music is to write a new poem. The best translators accept that loss is certain and decide, case by case, which loss the poem can best survive.

The author would most likely agree that:
prose translation is a purely mechanical task requiring no judgement
translators should always give priority to sound over sense
a faithful paraphrase is the ideal form of poetic translation
no translation of a poem can preserve everything that the original achieves
The author says 'loss is certain' in translating poetry; the other options overstate or contradict the passage.

Read the passage and answer the question.

A translator of poetry faces a choice that prose translators can often evade. Prose carries most of its meaning in its propositions, so a faithful paraphrase preserves most of what matters. In a poem, however, the sound, the line break and the ambiguity of a single word may be the meaning. To translate the propositions alone is to deliver a summary; to chase the music is to write a new poem. The best translators accept that loss is certain and decide, case by case, which loss the poem can best survive.

The phrase 'which loss the poem can best survive' implies that translators should:
judge which elements are least essential to a particular poem's effect
avoid translating poems whose meaning depends on sound
translate only the literal propositions of every poem
add new material to make up for every feature that is lost
Choosing which loss a poem 'can best survive' means deciding, case by case, what the poem can most afford to give up.

Read the passage and answer the question.

Cities have long planted trees for shade, but planners now value them for a subtler reason. A street tree cools its surroundings less by blocking sunlight than by transpiring water, which absorbs heat as it evaporates. A tree's cooling benefit therefore depends on its access to water: a drought-stressed tree closes its pores and cools far less, precisely during the hot, dry spells when cooling is most needed. Planting programmes that count trees but ignore soil volume and irrigation may therefore deliver less relief than their numbers suggest.

Which of the following is best supported by the passage?
Shade from trees plays no role in cooling cities
Two cities with the same number of street trees may get very different cooling benefits from them
Drought-stressed trees make streets hotter than streets with no trees at all
Irrigating street trees costs more than planting new ones
Since cooling depends on water access, equal tree counts can yield unequal cooling; the other options are extreme or unsupported.

The last sentence of the passage primarily serves to:
introduce a new scientific mechanism of cooling
reject the idea that trees cool cities at all
draw a practical implication for how tree-planting programmes should be assessed
summarise the history of urban tree planting
It applies the preceding explanation to planting programmes, warning that tree counts alone overstate relief.

Choose the option that best captures the essence of the paragraph.

Most consumers say they prefer ethically produced goods, yet sales data rarely match these stated preferences. The gap is often blamed on hypocrisy, but a simpler explanation exists: at the moment of purchase, price and convenience are visible and immediate, whereas ethical attributes are abstract and must be researched. Preferences that require effort to act upon lose out to those that do not, even when sincerely held.
Consumers who claim to prefer ethical goods are largely hypocritical.
Ethical goods fail to sell mainly because they are priced higher than ordinary goods.
The gap between stated ethical preferences and actual purchases reflects the unequal effort needed to act on different preferences, not necessarily insincerity.
Sales data are an unreliable measure of what consumers actually prefer.
The paragraph rejects the hypocrisy explanation and attributes the gap to the effort required to act on ethical preferences.
